topics.title: 课程作业
topics.summary: 是否、何时及如何使用生成式 AI 由各课程教师决定并写入课程大纲；学生须遵守课程和院系规定。直接复制输出、把 AI 输出（包括改写或意译后的输出）当作自己的成果，或超出教师限定范围，均构成学术诚信违规。部分院系更严格：艺术与考古学系禁止在课程作业中用 AI 生成、起草或润色文字，除非教师书面准许并要求披露的例外。
topics.scope: 依《权利、规则与责任》2.4 和课程规定逐门课决定；院系规则可能更严。

claims.text: Princeton's Office of the Dean of the College requires faculty to set clear expectations for whether, when and how generative AI can be used and to state them in the course syllabus; all students are expected to disclose their generative AI use and not pass off AI-generated content as their own, and faculty may provide their own disclosure template or use the standard one.

evidence.quote: Faculty must set clear expectations for whether, when, and how generative AI can be used and state those expectations in the course syllabus. Work created with the assistance of AI tools should never be a proxy for original work. All students are expected to abide by scholarly integrity expectations for appropriate generative AI use, which include disclosing their use of generative AI and not passing off AI-generated content as their own work.

claims.text: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities states that students must adhere to course and departmental generative AI policies, and that inappropriate uses on work submitted for an academic requirement - directly copying output, representing AI output as their own (including rewording or paraphrasing it), exceeding the instructor's parameters, or failing to disclose use (including use for rewording, paraphrasing or editing) - constitute academic integrity violations.

evidence.quote: Students are responsible for adhering to course and departmental policies regarding the use of generative AI. Inappropriate uses of generative AI on any work submitted to fulfill an academic requirement, such as directly copying the output, representing output generated by or derived from generative AI as their own (including rewording or paraphrasing output from generative AI and representing it as their own), exceeding the parameters of use specified by the instructor, or failing to disclose its use (including the use of generative AI for rewording, paraphrasing or editing) constitute violations of academic integrity.

claims.text: Princeton's Dean of the College stated in the Fall 2023 memo that the decision to allow, limit or prohibit generative AI in a course or in undergraduate independent work remains with the faculty. evidence.quote: First and foremost, the decision to allow, limit, or prohibit generative AI in a course or in undergraduate independent work will remain our faculty’s. Faculty members have the discretion to set their own generative AI policy for their courses.

claims.text: Princeton's Department of Art and Archaeology prohibits using AI as a text-generation tool in coursework, final examinations and independent projects: students may not submit AI-generated text, use AI-generated text as a draft they then modify or paraphrase, or use generative AI to edit and revise their work. Instructors may grant exceptions for a course assignment with written disclosure, but exceptions will never be made for the junior paper or senior thesis. This department rule is stricter than general course-by-course permission.

evidence.quote: As a result, the Department of Art & Archaeology explicitly prohibits the use of AI as a text-generation tool in the writing of coursework, final examinations, and independent projects alike.
evidence.title: History of Art Independent Work Guide: Policy on Generative Artificial Intelligence
evidence.location: Policy on Generative Artificial Intelligence; lines 509-509 of captured page text

evidence.quote: A student may not rely on AI-generated text as a rough or partial draft, which they then modify or paraphrase before submitting it as their own work; likewise, a student may not use generative AI in editing and revising their work.
evidence.title: History of Art Independent Work Guide: Policy on Generative Artificial Intelligence
evidence.location: Policy on Generative Artificial Intelligence; lines 509-509 of captured page text

evidence.quote: That said, an instructor may wish to grant exceptions for AI use in a course assignment as long as the student strictly follows the instructor’s guidelines and discloses the specific use in writing. Exceptions will never be made for the junior paper or the senior thesis.

claims.text: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities (2.4) states that generative AI is not a source; where an instructor permits generative AI, students must disclose its use rather than cite or acknowledge it. Scholarly Integrity guidance says failure to disclose, even in a course where AI is permitted, is a scholarly integrity violation, and offers a disclosure template.

claims.text: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities (2.4.5), as quoted by Scholarly Integrity, provides that undergraduates may use only Princeton-authorized academic support: when completing any work to fulfil an academic requirement (homework, problem sets, quizzes or examinations), undergraduates may not use non-Princeton tutoring resources, including AI tutoring bots. This applies to work done for academic requirements; it is not a ban on all AI-assisted study.

evidence.quote: When completing any work to fulfill an academic requirement (such as homework assignments, problem sets, quizzes or examinations of any kind), undergraduate students may not make use of any non-Princeton tutoring resources, including paid or unpaid tutors, independent tutoring services, or AI tutoring bots.

additionalTopics.title: 教学指导
additionalTopics.summary: 普林斯顿大学大学学院院长办公室（ODOC）要求教师必须就生成式 AI 能否使用、何时及如何使用确立明确预期，并写入课程教学大纲；同时所有学生均须遵守学术诚信规范，包括披露生成式 AI 的使用，严禁将 AI 生成内容冒充为自己的原创作品。
additionalTopics.scope: ODOC 课程规程与政策；面向教师的大纲强制要求与披露规范指引。

claims.text: Princeton's Office of the Dean of the College requires faculty to set clear expectations for whether, when and how generative AI can be used and to state them in the course syllabus; all students are expected to disclose their generative AI use and not pass off AI-generated content as their own, and faculty may provide their own disclosure template or use the standard one.

evidence.quote: Faculty must set clear expectations for whether, when, and how generative AI can be used and state those expectations in the course syllabus. Work created with the assistance of AI tools should never be a proxy for original work. All students are expected to abide by scholarly integrity expectations for appropriate generative AI use, which include disclosing their use of generative AI and not passing off AI-generated content as their own work.
evidence.title: Course Procedures & Policies (Office of the Dean of the College)
evidence.location: Students and Generative AI; lines 212-212 of captured page text

additionalTopics.title: 安全与采购
additionalTopics.summary: 依据普林斯顿大学《生成式 AI 工具使用政策》，如果您正在考虑采购生成式 AI 工具，或者现有的信息技术工具获得了生成式 AI 功能，第一步就是预约安排“架构与安全审查”（ASR）。
additionalTopics.scope: OIT 生成式 AI 工具使用政策；关于生成式 AI 工具采购或功能的架构与安全审查（ASR）规程。

claims.text: Under Princeton's Generative AI Tools Use Policy, anyone considering procuring a generative AI tool, or whose existing IT tool gains generative AI capabilities, must first schedule an Architecture & Security Review (ASR); tools endorsed through ASR then go through Procurement/OIT contract review.

evidence.quote: If you are considering procuring a generative AI tool or if an existing information technology tool acquires generative AI capabilities, the first step is to schedule an Architecture & Security Review (ASR).
